# Draft:The Enclosure (Grand Teton monument)

"The Enclosure," also called "Bishéesh's Enclosure," is an oval-shaped man-made formation of large, flat, Granite stones located in the Teton mountains.
Location
The formation itself sits at around 12,000 feet (3,600 meters) in elevation. It forms the "left shoulder" or West buttress of the Grand Teton peak.
History
When the Washburn-Langford-Doane expedition party climbed the Grand Teton in 1872 they believed they were making history by being the first to ever summit it. In the course of their climb, they found the structure.
Spiritual Significance
People of the Crow, or Apsáalooke, Tribe know and build structures like these, and they call them "fasting beds." There are many located throughout traditional Crow lands in Wyoming and Montana.
